acceptance: docs/internal/nightly-t3.md and nightly-v2.yml list the same domains; the browser domain is removed from the plan and its coverage is owned by dlv2-site-browser-check
t3:sql-execution-gate-obt, drift-gate and throughput-signal failures each reach a per-domain issue/label or an explicit infrastructure alert; skipped drift is distinguishable from a failed selection
Former needs are reconciled with primary evidence recorded here: perf (issue #2778 closed, PR #2859), docker (PR #3150, issue #2906 closed), drift (issue #2471 closed or each failing drift job fixed)
2-3 workflow_dispatch runs of nightly-v2 (t3:cloud off) in which every non-skipped domain passes, with run ids and a job-level comparison against the legacy nightly recorded
Duration handling matches dlv2-13a (aggregate gate), cloud stays opt-in, and the owner response policy is documented
context: 2026-10-27: dispatch #31 (2026-10-20) is the only green run of 40; no scheduled nightly-v2 run has been green. 2026-10-26/27 fixes: corpus mirror #3568 merged, Windows PR leg #3548 merged (module-state-guard home-dir env). Owner decision 2026-10-27: browser domain is ported to the site repo (dlv2-site-browser-check); Explorer-token lint retired. Perf, docker and drift needs were removed from needs because evidence above replaces them.
description:
AUDIT 2026-10-27 (owner-adjudicated, advisor-reviewed): the acceptance and context sections supersede this description wherever they differ. Historical text below is kept for reference.

New .github/workflows/nightly-v2.yml (renamed to nightly.yml when the old one retires in dlv2-70) at trunk tip with separate jobs and separate failure labels: t3:docker (postgres, clickhouse, trino from docker-integration.yml), t3:cloud (credentialed, optional), t3:perf (perf-smoke), t3:matrix (Python 3.11-3.14 x Linux/macOS/Windows from cross-platform-validation.yml), t3:browser (firefox/webkit explorer), t3:extension (duckdb-datasketches from extension-smoke.yml), t3:install (pypi-latest installability from release-canary.yml), t3:drift (weekly: corpus-drift, pricing-data drift, submission-validator drift, cross-surface baseline autodetect); plus quarantined tests and durations-file refresh. Each failing domain opens/updates one issue with its own label and owner. An open t3:* issue marked release-blocking blocks release.yml (dlv2-51). The nightly trunk-tip run replaces the re-run that the retired develop-post-merge workflow did; per-push checks on develop now run in trunk.yml.
